title: Levothyroxine treatment response of cardiometabolic biomarkers in older adults with subclinical hypothyroidism
authors: Ao L, Noordam R, Trompet S, van Vliet NA, Sattar N, Rodondi N, et al.
journal: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism
population: Post hoc analysis of TRUST and IEMO 80-plus participants aged 65 or older with subclinical hypothyroidism and stored samples; median age 75 years, 48% women, median TSH 6.44 mIU/l; 142 randomised to levothyroxine
funder: L.A. is supported by the China Scholarship Council. This work was supported by a research grant (666869, THYRAGE) from the European Union Horizon 2020 program. The IEMO trial was supported by ZonMw and the Swiss National Science Foundation; the TRUST trial by the European Union FP7-HEALTH-2011 program and the Swiss National Science Foundation.
inKindSupport: Levothyroxine and matching placebo supplied free of charge by the healthcare business of Merck KGaA, acknowledged as nonfinancial support.
authorConflicts: One author reported consulting or speaker fees and grant support from many pharmaceutical companies, including AbbVie, outside the submitted work.
result: Levothyroxine against placebo at 12 months: apolipoprotein B -0.03 g/l (95% CI -0.07 to 0.00), total cholesterol -0.17 mmol/l (-0.34 to 0.00), non-HDL cholesterol -0.15 (-0.31 to 0.00), remnant cholesterol -0.09 (-0.16 to -0.01), LDL cholesterol -0.07 (-0.15 to 0.02), triglycerides -0.07 (-0.15 to 0.01); the authors concluded there were no effects overall. In 27 participants with TSH of 10 mIU/l or more, lipid changes were nominally favourable but not significant after correction for multiple testing.
